title: South Carolina's 6th Congressional District election, 2026
description: South Carolina's 6th Congressional District election pits 34-year incumbent Rep. James Clyburn (D) against Republican nominee John Peterson and Alliance Party candidate Joseph Oddo. The district, which includes all or parts of 15 counties in central and eastern South Carolina, has been represented by Clyburn since 1993 and is rated as Solidly Democratic by the Cook Political Report. Clyburn, the 85-year-old former House Majority Whip who is seeking an 18th term, easily won his Democratic primary with 90.3% of the vote, while Peterson secured the Republican nomination with 74% against Maurice Washington. A GOP effort to redraw the district's lines to create a 7-0 Republican delegation failed in May 2026.
polling_note: No general election opinion polls were found for this race. The Cook Political Report rated the district as Solidly Democratic prior to the primary.

candidates.name: James E. Clyburn
candidates.summary: James E. Clyburn has represented South Carolina's 6th Congressional District since 1993 and is the longest-serving member of Congress in South Carolina history. He previously served as House Majority Whip (2007-2010, 2019-2022) and Assistant Democratic Leader, and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2024. Clyburn is widely credited with reviving Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign through his endorsement before the South Carolina primary.

candidates.name: John Peterson
candidates.summary: John Peterson is a banquet supervisor at Embassy Suites in North Charleston and a political newcomer who won the Republican nomination for South Carolina's 6th Congressional District with 74% of the primary vote. He describes himself as a 'common sense conservative' and emphasizes fiscally conservative policies, voter ID requirements, and reducing the national debt. Peterson holds a bachelor's degree in mathematics from the State University of New York.

candidates.name: Joseph Oddo
candidates.summary: Joseph Oddo is the Alliance Party nominee for South Carolina's 6th Congressional District. A mergers and acquisitions advisor and writer, Oddo has run for Congress multiple times in both Virginia and South Carolina as a third-party candidate. He advocates for election reform including instant-runoff voting, balancing the federal budget, and protecting natural resources. Oddo holds a bachelor's degree in public policy from Penn State University.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polls exist for this race, capping confidence at medium. However, the fundamental indicators are overwhelming: Cook Political Report rates the district Solidly Democratic; Clyburn has held the seat for 34 years (since 1993) and won his 2026 primary with 90.3%; the Republican nominee is a political newcomer and banquet supervisor with no prior elected office; the Alliance candidate is a perennial third-party contender. Critically, a May 2026 GOP effort to redraw the district to create a 7-0 Republican delegation failed, confirming the current lines remain heavily Democratic. Without polling, there is elevated uncertainty about precise margin, but the district's structural partisan lean and Clyburn's entrenched incumbency support a safe Democratic forecast.
